name: Social networking
title: Why SixDegrees failed, and when social networks became viable
question: Why did SixDegrees fail, and when did social networks become viable?
answer: SixDegrees.com (1997) had the social graph first: profiles, friend lists and messaging. It was sold in 1999 and shut in 2001. Few people had broadband or digital photos, so there was little to share and slow pages to share it on. Friendster, MySpace and Facebook (2002-2004) arrived as US broadband passed 7-13 lines per 100 people.
verdict_reason: Broadband and digital photos crossed around 2003; three social networks launched within two years.

constraint.name: Broadband and digital photo upload
constraint.detail: A social network is mostly photos and frequent visits; on dial-up neither works.

crossing.text: US fixed broadband passes 9 lines per 100 people (World Bank); digital cameras go mainstream.
